title: OMORI
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Manga adaptation of the psychological horror video game OMORI. Sunny has not left his house since something happened four years ago; days before his family moves away, his childhood friend Kel draws him back out into town, and old friends and a buried past resurface (K Manga blurb). ANN notes the central mystery involves the death of a friend, Mari, which split the group apart; the English edition is rated T (ANN).
life_message: Facing a painful past honestly, with friends, is the way out of isolation and guilt.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflict is about guilt and honesty, not defending standing (ANN; MU Regret).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Teens largely on their own in town; family move frames the plot (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friend group matters more than family in summaries (MU Reunited Friends).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Peer friendships, little adult authority shown.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Psychological, not religious, framing of grief (MU Psychological).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Emotional healing and personal truth are the stakes (MU Overcoming the Past).

folkways.japan: Sunny's long withdrawal echoes the Japanese hikikomori phenomenon, though the source game is American-made and set in a nonspecific town.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it 'genuine and deeply personal' and 'heartwrenching'; no comment on preachiness (to verify).
delivery.note: Themes of guilt and recovery come through the mystery and the friends' reunion rather than stated lessons, as far as the sources show.

winners_losers: Sympathy rests with Sunny and the estranged friends as they reckon with Mari's death; isolation and secrecy are the forces the story works against.
